prompt: Express $z=1-\sqrt3\,i$ in the form $r\operatorname{cis}\theta$, where $r>0$ and $-\pi<\theta\le\pi$.
markscheme:
$r=\sqrt{1+3}=2$ **(A1)**

$z$ is in the fourth quadrant and $\tan\theta=-\sqrt3$, so $\theta=-\dfrac\pi3$ **(A1)**

$z=2\operatorname{cis}\left(-\dfrac\pi3\right)$ **(A1)**

concept: Products and quotients in polar form
prompt:
Let $z_1=4\operatorname{cis}\dfrac\pi3$ and $z_2=2\operatorname{cis}\dfrac\pi6$.

**(a)** Find $z_1z_2$ in Cartesian form. **[2]**

**(b)** Find $\dfrac{z_1}{z_2}$ in Cartesian form. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** Multiply moduli, add arguments: $8\operatorname{cis}\dfrac\pi2$ **(M1)** $=8i$ **(A1)**

**(b)** Divide moduli, subtract arguments: $2\operatorname{cis}\dfrac\pi6$ **(M1)** $=\sqrt3+i$ **(A1)**

prompt:
**(a)** Use $e^{i\theta}=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta$ to show that $e^{i\pi}+1=0$. **[1]**

**(b)** Show that $\cos\theta=\dfrac{e^{i\theta}+e^{-i\theta}}{2}$. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $e^{i\pi}=\cos\pi+i\sin\pi=-1$, so $e^{i\pi}+1=0$ **(A1)(AG)**

**(b)** $e^{-i\theta}=\cos(-\theta)+i\sin(-\theta)=\cos\theta-i\sin\theta$ **(M1)** (cos is even, sin is odd)

Adding: $e^{i\theta}+e^{-i\theta}=2\cos\theta$ **(A1)(AG)**

concept: Geometric meaning of sums and products
prompt:
Let $w=2e^{i\pi/4}$.

**(a)** Describe the single transformation of the Argand plane that maps any $z$ to $wz$. **[2]**

**(b)** The points $0$, $z_1$, $z_2$ and $z_1+z_2$ are plotted on an Argand diagram. Describe the shape they form and explain why. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $|wz|=2|z|$ and $\arg(wz)=\arg z+\frac\pi4$ **(M1)**: an enlargement with scale factor 2 about the origin combined with an anticlockwise rotation of $\frac\pi4$ about the origin (a spiral similarity) **(A1)**

**(b)** A parallelogram **(A1)**: complex numbers add like vectors, so $z_1+z_2$ is reached by moving along $z_1$ then along a vector equal to $z_2$ **(R1)**.
